phenomena.label: Coordinate Structure Constraint — embedded negative na(d)
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may license the negative particle na(d) in only one conjunct, failing to propagate it across the coordinate structure.
phenomena.note: The embedded negative declarative na(d) must be repeated in every conjunct of a coordinate structure.

phenomena.label: Anti-agreement effect
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs tend to agree the verb with the extracted plural subject, whereas Welsh wh-subject extraction forces default 3sg.
phenomena.note: In subject wh-questions the verb stays 3rd sg with no agreement for the extracted plural subject.

phenomena.label: Possessor extraction ban (pied-piping)
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may strand the possessed noun and extract only the possessor, which Welsh disallows in favour of pied-piping the whole DP.
phenomena.note: A possessor cannot be extracted from a DP; the whole DP must pied-pipe.

phenomena.label: Superiority in multiple wh-questions
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may front the object wh-word over the subject wh-word, violating the subject>object ordering.
phenomena.note: With multiple wh-words the subject wh fronts and the object wh stays in situ (subject > object).

phenomena.label: Resumptive pronoun ban in subject/object position
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may insert an overt resumptive pronoun at subject or object extraction sites where Welsh requires a gap.
phenomena.note: Overt resumptive pronouns are impossible in subject and direct-object positions; the gap strategy is used instead.

phenomena.label: Relative clause subject gap
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may spell out an overt pronoun at the subject relativisation site, which Welsh excludes.
phenomena.note: In relative clauses an overt pronoun is excluded at the subject relativisation site.

phenomena.label: Preposition agreement in object-of-preposition relatives
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may pied-pipe the PP with a wh-word rather than use the required inflected preposition agreement.
phenomena.note: Relatives on the object of a preposition require agreement on the preposition; pied-piping the PP is impossible.

phenomena.label: Overt wh in non-restrictive adjunct relatives
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may omit the obligatory overt wh-word in non-restrictive adjunct relatives.
phenomena.note: Non-restrictive adjunct relatives require an overt wh-word.

phenomena.label: Propositional adverbs in focus position
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may combine a focus-position propositional adverb with an affirmative particle fe/mi, which is banned.
phenomena.note: Propositional adverbs such as hwyrach 'probably' sit in focus position and cannot co-occur with affirmative particles fe/mi.

phenomena.label: No agreement with focused pronominal subject
phenomena.hypothesis: LMs may inflect the verb to agree with a focused pronominal subject, but Welsh keeps default 3sg.
phenomena.note: With a focused pronominal subject the verb stays default 3rd sg with no agreement.

phenomena.label: VSO default agreement
phenomena.hypothesis: With a non-pronominal subject the finite verb appears in default 3rd singular regardless of subject number.
phenomena.note: Gwelodd (3sg) vs Gwelon (3pl) with plural lexical subject y bechgyn

phenomena.label: Embedded bod-clauses
phenomena.hypothesis: Embedded affirmative declarative complements require non-finite bod rather than present-tense mae.
phenomena.note: bod = non-finite be; mae = present indicative, ungrammatical in complement

phenomena.label: Aspectual particle order
phenomena.hypothesis: When perfect wedi and progressive yn co-occur, wedi must precede yn.
phenomena.note: wedi = perfect, yn = progressive

phenomena.label: No fronting of aspectual yn
phenomena.hypothesis: The aspectual particle yn cannot be included in a fronted constituent.
phenomena.note: fronted verb-noun appears bare, without yn

phenomena.label: Gwneud clause fronting
phenomena.hypothesis: Non-finite gwneud requires a fronted complement and cannot take an in-situ verbal complement.
phenomena.note: gwneud = do; complement must be fronted

phenomena.label: Negative pronoun object
phenomena.hypothesis: Simple VSO clauses negate via a negative pronoun object, but gwneud-clauses cannot.
phenomena.note: neb = anyone/no one

phenomena.label: Adverb placement
phenomena.hypothesis: An adverb may intervene between the verb and an indefinite subject but not between the verb and a definite subject.
phenomena.note: wastad/yfory = adverbs; definite Emrys blocks intervention

phenomena.label: Reflexive binding (Principle A)
phenomena.hypothesis: A subject can antecede a reflexive object but an object cannot antecede a reflexive subject.
phenomena.note: ei hun = himself

phenomena.label: Expletive hi extraposition
phenomena.hypothesis: Expletive hi with an extraposed clausal subject is required; a clausal subject in situ is ungrammatical.
phenomena.note: hi = expletive it; clausal subject extraposed

phenomena.label: Expletive yna distribution
phenomena.hypothesis: The expletive yna may appear only between a finite verb and its associated noun phrase.
phenomena.note: yna = existential expletive there

phenomena.label: Adjective agreement in numeral phrases
phenomena.hypothesis: Adjectives in numeral phrases must appear in the singular form.
phenomena.note: ifainc/eraill are plural forms; singular ifanc/arall required after numerals

phenomena.label: Standalone adjective requires pronominal head un
phenomena.hypothesis: A singular adjective cannot stand alone with the article; the pronominal head un is required.
phenomena.note: glas blue needs un as nominal head under the article

phenomena.label: Definiteness in possessor chains
phenomena.hypothesis: In a possessor chain only the final possessor bears the definite article, making the whole phrase definite.
phenomena.note: no article on non-final nouns; whole phrase is definite via final y

phenomena.label: Agreement with pronominal vs lexical subjects
phenomena.hypothesis: The verb agrees with a pronominal subject but stays default 3sg with a non-pronominal subject.
phenomena.note: plural pronoun nhw triggers plural gwelon; lexical DP takes 3sg gwelodd

phenomena.label: No agreement with coordinate subjects
phenomena.hypothesis: The verb cannot agree with a whole coordinate subject, even when both conjuncts are pronouns; default 3sg is used.
phenomena.note: coordinated ti a fi takes 2sg default gwelaist, not plural gwelon

phenomena.label: Negative Dependent Constraint
phenomena.hypothesis: Sentential negation requires the adverb ddim.
phenomena.note: negative n-word dim licensed by ddim

phenomena.label: dim versus ddim after negatives
phenomena.hypothesis: The quantifier dim may follow a negative subject, but the adverb ddim cannot.
phenomena.note: ddim is barred after the negative subject neb

phenomena.label: mo before definite objects in negatives
phenomena.hypothesis: The adverb ddim cannot be immediately followed by an object; Welsh uses mo instead.
phenomena.note: mo = contraction of ddim + o before a definite object

phenomena.label: N-words in imperatives require paid/peidiwch
phenomena.hypothesis: N-words are impossible in the imperative unless paid/peidiwch is used.
phenomena.note: neb needs negative auxiliary paid in imperatives

phenomena.label: Obligatory agreement clitic in passives
phenomena.hypothesis: The agreement clitic is obligatory in passives.
phenomena.note: ei clitic required before the non-finite verb daro

phenomena.label: No pronoun after passive non-finite verb
phenomena.hypothesis: The non-finite verb in a passive cannot be followed by a pronoun.
phenomena.note: resumptive pronoun o barred after ei daro

phenomena.label: Allomorphy of the conjunction and
phenomena.hypothesis: The conjunction and is ac before a vowel and a before a consonant.
phenomena.note: ac pre-vocalic, a pre-consonantal
